summary: Commissioned 1955 and abandoned in the 1980s; a September 2021 trip report still found a fire lookout on the summit near Princeton, BC.

facts.status_note: Poor condition. An undated visitor account says it has no windows or door and may fall over.

access.note: Reached by forest roads and a walk. The sources name no gate or permit and describe no closure of the lookout itself.

visit.trail_note: Stock 4x4 route, 31.5 km (19.6 mi) one way from Copper Mountain Road, per one trip report. The accounts disagree on whether the Wolf Creek road is open.

events.note: Commissioned in 1955, per an undated visitor account.
The account gives only the decade (the 1980s); 1980 is entered as a stand-in for that decade.
Trip report of September 2021 describes a fire lookout still on the summit.

evidence.supports: Lookout is in the Okanagan-Similkameen district
Overlooks the Similkameen valley from Agate Mountain near Princeton; abandoned B.C. forestry station
evidence.quote: Agate Fire Tower is an abandoned B.C. Forestry Station overlooking the Silmilkameen valley from Agate mountain, not far from Princeton, BC.

evidence.supports: Commissioned in 1955; in use every year through the fire season
evidence.quote: It was commissioned in 1955 and active every year during the 6 months of the forest fire season.

evidence.supports: Abandoned in the 1980s when new technology made staffing unfeasible
evidence.quote: It was eventually abandoned in the 1980s when new technology made having a staffed lookout unfeasible.

evidence.supports: Never adopted by the local community; has degraded each year
evidence.quote: The fire lookout has never been adopted/loved by the local community and has degraded further every year.

evidence.supports: Wood shed and outhouse on site
evidence.quote: has some other historical buildings on site including a wood shed and outhouse.

evidence.supports: All buildings, including the tower, near end of life
evidence.quote: All buildings including the lookout tower itself are in the final stages of life.

evidence.supports: No windows or door; may fall over
evidence.quote: At the moment there are no windows or door and it might not be long before the tower falls over completely.

sources.title: Agate Mountain Fire Lookout - Willis Creek FSR

notes_for_editor: Only one source gives a build year (1955) and the 1980s abandonment, and it is undated. A search for a 1955 Forest Service record found nothing. The 1980 abandonment event is a stand-in for the decade. Two undated accounts disagree on whether the Wolf Creek road is open. BC Archives photographs of the lookout (series GR-3263) were seen only in search snippets; their pages return a certificate error, so nothing from them is quoted. No source describes the tower's design or height. The record's brief has status, kind and access as unknown; the story uses standing, derelict, from the undated account and the September 2021 report.
